This modest neonatal weight, typical of estrildid finches, necessitates intensive biparental provisioning throughout the nestling period. The downy chicks depend entirely on their parents for thermoregulation and food delivery during the early stages of development, as they lack the motor coordination for independent feeding. The marked contrast between this initial mass and the adult body size underscores the substantial growth trajectory that must be completed before the young birds reach independence and eventual reproductive maturity.
